physicalNotes: Radius 1.18 Jupiter radii from the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated radius (its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, since HD 73344 d does not transit, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html): 84,360.6 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 2.55 Jupiter masses (Zhang et al. 2025, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2025AJ....169..200Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....169..200Z/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Zhang et al. 2025 (2025AJ....169..200Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ZHANG_ET_AL_2025): P 5823 d
sources.shape: Zhang et al. 2025 (2025AJ....169..200Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ZHANG_ET_AL_2025): a/R* derived from its semi-major axis 6.7 au and stellar radius 1.22 solar radii; inclination 59 +19 degrees, measured in the same fit
sources.eccentricity: Zhang et al. 2025 (2025AJ....169..200Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ZHANG_ET_AL_2025): e 0.18
sources.argumentOfPeriapsis: Zhang et al. 2025 (2025AJ....169..200Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ZHANG_ET_AL_2025): omega 58.9 degrees
sources.phase: Zhang et al. 2025 (2025AJ....169..200Z), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ZHANG_ET_AL_2025): periastron passage 2458061 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB
sources.orientation: Display convention: the NASA Exoplanet Archive carries no position angle for the orbit's node on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
